P1.evidence: Setter notes referenced and used twice ('I already heard a few things from Kim', and later the 23% body fat figure). Frame was three-part, not four — 'where you're at, where you want to go, see if we really fit in there' — missing what's in the way and what you need. Clean agreement ask, 'Sounds good?', and a textbook open question, 'What can we potentially help you out with, Scott?'

P2.evidence: Diet and energy were properly asked and produced real data — 'do you have an idea from what you're eating from like day-to-day basis?' got tracked macros, and 'How is your energy level throughout the day?' got the 10-hour fade. Age, height and weight were volunteered and only confirmed back, and body fat came from the setter rather than the call. Health conditions were never asked: the prospect volunteered AFib, a family history of heart issues and blood pressure issues, and the rep did not respond to any of it — a miss by the volunteered-information rule and a safety gap besides. Sleep was never mentioned at all. Injury probe ran ('are you stiff and do you have some mobility things already?') but the rotator cuff repair it surfaced was never explored. Current training was known in outline but actual days trained per week was never established, and results from current training were never asked.

P3.evidence: The best-run phase. The bridge question landed hard — 'you're 62, it's not like you're in terrible shape... Why do you feel like, no, I'm not happy with it, I want it to be better?' — and produced three minutes of unforced depth about outliving his wife, Medicare, identity and not wanting to retire and sit. 'How would that be for you when you actually do achieve that goal?' pulled out the backpacking trip and the century ride. But 'Who else does that impact?' was never asked, with a wife, four and a half grandchildren and a hiking friend all sitting on the table — the single cheapest miss on the call. The reflect-back at 00:18:50 summarised the surface goals accurately but never made the 'this isn't really about the weight' turn.

P4.evidence: Skipped entirely. Not one past-attempt or root-cause question was asked. The prospect handed the rep the opening unprompted — he has self-programmed since 2005, owns the kettlebells already, and said 'I get on the bike, but it's like, okay, here we are, on the bike, big deal' and 'looking to get a little more of an outside perspective' — and the rep never asked why twenty years of self-direction has not produced the result, or what would be different this time. Because he was volunteered rather than asked, none of it credits.

P5.evidence: The settle question ran cleanly — 'are you willing to settle for a life where you don't get like that longevity because you're not actually doubling down on it?' — and got a firm 'No, life would be a drag.' But the two-year cost-of-inaction picture was never painted, so there was no downside to settle against; the rep worked the upside future instead. 'Why not?' was not asked, the prospect elaborated on his own. The line in the sand was asserted rather than requested: 'it sounds like you're ready for yourself. You have made that commitment to yourself.'

P6.evidence: The go-all-in question ran well: 'do you feel like when we get those all three in place, that there would be any reason for you not to be able to get to the part where you're going to have that longevity...' — answered 'No, I think I can do that.' Sequencing was off, though: the playbook wants a genuine verbal yes before presenting anything, and the full three-pillar presentation ran first, with only a soft assertion of commitment beforehand. Belief in getting there with the right structure and the right person was never directly tested. He correctly did not price until he had a yes.

P11.evidence: Steps 2, 3 and 4 were run properly and in order: Trevor booked for Wednesday 18:15 with the invite confirmed received, the agreement email located on his business address and signed live on the call ('Only have to sign it in one place... Did that'), and the welcome email, Skool link and onboarding questionnaire all confirmed, plus the tracking app. Step 1 is only half done — the first card attempt was declined, $3,000 went through, and the remaining $3,000 was pushed to an unscheduled 'next week' link with the bank limit never confirmed. The rep even offered to defer it a month before the prospect chose next week.

objection_plays.detail: No hesitation or think-about-it at any point. Price was accepted within seconds.
No spouse-consult trigger. Notable inversion: the wife was raised as an obstacle to training rather than to the purchase, and he treated the decision as entirely his own.
No money objection. 'Fair enough. I can do that.' The later card-limit issue was mechanical, not a value or affordability objection, and correctly was not treated as one.
The opposite — he volunteered that now is the right time because his schedule and business finally allow it.

Card declined and a bank limit below $6,000. No scripted play exists for a willing buyer whose card cannot carry the full amount. The rep improvised well — split to $3,000 and captured it immediately — but then let the balance float to an unscheduled 'next week' and even offered 'next month' as an option. A payment-friction play that fixes a date and sends the second link before hanging up would have closed this properly.

Script gap: an undisclosed-risk medical history in an otherwise ideal buyer. The prospect stated he has had AFib, has a family history of heart issues and blood pressure issues, and has an internist watching him closely — all at 00:04:54 and 00:16:05. The playbook has no screening step and no clearance protocol, so nothing prompted the rep to react, and he did not. This is the same clinical blind spot already flagged from the Tyron Giuliani call, but here it cuts the other way: instead of losing a qualified prospect, the programme sold intense conditioning to a 63-year-old cardiac patient without a single question about it.

notes: Richard built genuine rapport and ran an excellent Phase 3 — the 'why now, why not settle for it' sequence produced the real motivation and effectively sold the call. But he skipped Phase 4 entirely and half of Phase 2, so he never learned why two decades of competent self-programming has not worked, which is exactly the argument this prospect needed and exactly what he will question in month three. Two concrete coaching points: ask 'who else does that impact' when a prospect has already named grandchildren and a wife, and never let a declined card end the call without a fixed date and a sent link for the balance. Separately, escalate the unaddressed AFib disclosure — that is a process gap above the rep's pay grade.
